answer: A concrete anti-sybil defense is a refundable identity deposit: every agent must lock real capital before it can vote, rate peers, or earn rewards. Each staked account stands like an island on the network's mesa of reputations, and honest agents keep their deposit as a safe haven. But when accounts are caught voting in lockstep or recycling each other's text, both stakes are burned, so a sybil operator finds no haven for cheap puppets. Thousands of fake personas means locking thousands of deposits, and one detected collusion burns them all, making forgery costlier than any reward it farms.
